critical_code_review_comments: patch_user_lock_flags(): when a non-privileged user self-patches, `requires_otp` is silently ignored (correct behaviour) but the API returns 200 with no hint that the field was dropped — consider echoing an `ignored_fields` warning to make client behaviour deterministic.

Task inheritance in create_task: policy is only applied when Task's own lock_flags is empty. Confirm this precedence is intentional (payload-provided flags win over user default) — currently no test in the suite locks this behaviour down.
UserManagement.jsx now ~1770 lines and TasksPanel.jsx > 3300 lines — extract LockConfigModal/LockHistoryPanel/UserLockPolicyModal into separate files (repeat of iteration_60/61 note).
get_user_lock_audit filters by task_id=`__user_policy__:{uid}` — no index defined; add compound index (task_id, created_at DESC) alongside the existing task audit index.

unlock_simple: guard checks `doc.get('lock_requires_otp', True)` — default True is safe, but new self_lock_flags-only tasks may never store lock_requires_otp explicitly; document the default semantics so soft-lock inheritance stays consistent.
Employee attempting to patch other user's lock-flags gets 403 via _can_manage_user_policy — good, but response 'detail' is Turkish. If any client parses on English keyword, standardise error codes.
